question.:question/problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x, y) = 2x^{2} + 2y^{2} - y$ that passes through the point where $(x, y) = (0, 1)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x^{2}+2y^{2}-y)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x^{2}+2y^{2}-y)\,j \\  & =(4x+0+0)\,i+(0+4y-1)\,j \\  & =(4x)\,i+(4y-1)\,j \\ ∇f(0,1) & =(4(0))\,i+(4(1)-1)\,j \\  & =3\,j\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(0,1)}{‖∇f(0,1)‖} & =\frac{3\,j}{\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(3)^{2}}} \\  & =j\end{aligned}
